review_candidates.description: Vacancy #: 7745 Unit: ESARO - Zimbabwe Corporate Services (ZW) Organisation: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Location: Zimbabwe Country Office, Harare, Zimbabwe Reporting to: Programme Officer, FLL Programme, Malawi Work percentage: 100% Grade: P2 Expected start date: 01 January 2027 Type of contract: Fixed-term (up to 24 months) Closing date: 10 December 2026 BACKGROUND THE SENIOR GRANTS AND FINANCE OFFICER IS A LOCAL POSITION IN MALAWI AND WILL BE BASED IN LILONGWE WITH TRAVELS ACROSS THE COUNTRY AND THE REGION. Background IUCN's Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO), through the Malawi Country Office, is seeking a Senior Grants and Finance Officer to be based in Lilongwe, Malawi, to support the implementation of the EU-funded project “Titukule Ntchito Zokopa Alendo Titukule Malawi” (TAZA – Tourism Enterprise Development for local and national prosperity in Malawi). TAZA is one component of the broader EU Green Heart of Africa Programme (Component 3: Tourism) and supports the development of viable, locally-led ecotourism enterprises in priority tourism hotspots through a matching grants scheme, combined with capacity building, mentorship and investment promotion. As the Malawi Country Office and its grant portfolio continue to grow, the position will provide a level of financial and grants management experience commensurate with the increasing scale and complexity of the country programme, with scope for the responsibilities of the position to expand accordingly over time. The Senior Grants and Finance Officer will provide day-to-day financial management and grants administration support to the project, working closely with the Programme Manager, the Regional Grants and Contracts Manager, and the Regional Accounting Compliance Manager, and will support the processing, verification and reporting of financial support provided to third parties (matching grants) in compliance with the EU Financial Regulation and IUCN policies and procedures. This position will form part of the Regional Grants Team and, as such, the postholder will be expected to contribute to and support other grants-related assignments and activities across the region, as required. Job Description MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES: The Senior Grants and Finance Officer will ensure effective day-to-day financial and grants management for the TAZA project, including review and verification of financial reports and supporting documentation, oversight of grant-related financial processes, and application of segregation of duties to strengthen internal controls, in full compliance with both EU donor and IUCN policies and procedures. As a senior member of the country team, the position is also expected to exercise sound independent judgement, provide guidance to junior staff on financial and grants matters, and progressively take on a broader financial and grants oversight role across the Malawi country programme as it grows. Specific Duties The specific duties and responsibilities of the Senior Grants and Finance Officer will be: Financial Monitoring and Reporting; Reviews and verifies financial reports, transactions and supporting documentation for the TAZA project in line with IUCN and EU financial regulations. Applies segregation of duties and internal control procedures to safeguard project funds and strengthen the project's overall control environment. Supports the processing of pre-financing, interim and final payments to matching-grant recipients, suppliers and service providers, ensuring completeness and accuracy of supporting documentation. Prepares monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports for the project, including narratives explaining variances against approved budgets, for independent review and approval by the Regional Accounting Compliance Manager. Prepares cash-flow forecasts and supports requests for funds (pre-financing and instalment payments) to the EU Delegation, and tracks exchange-rate gains and losses (MWK/EUR) and the eligibility of taxes, including VAT, in line with the contract. Maintains complete, orderly and audit-ready financial and grant files, ensuring supporting documents are retained for the period required under the EU grant agreement and IUCN records retention policy. Prepares and records financial transactions and reconciles project accounts in IUCN's accounting system. Supports the expenditure verification and audit processes, including the end-of-project audit, liaising with auditors and providing requested documentation. Coordinates closely with the Regional Accounting Compliance Manager and the Regional Grants and Contracts Manager to ensure sound financial governance, accountability and timely reporting to the EU Delegation. Grants Management (Matching Grants Scheme); Supports the operational management of the TAZA matching grants scheme, including appraisal, contracting, disbursement and closure processes, in accordance with the EU Financial Regulation and the project's Grant Operational Manual. Verifies that co-financing contributions (cash and in-kind) declared by grantees meet the minimum thresholds and eligibility criteria set out in the call for proposals and are properly valued and documented. Supports due diligence on prospective grantees, including verification of financial capacity, eligibility and compliance documentation. Tracks graduated, tranche-based disbursement of grants against agreed milestones and flags variances or delays for management action. Reviews grantee financial and expenditure reports to confirm compliance with grant agreements and donor requirements. Maintains the grants register and tracking tools, ensuring accurate and up-to-date records of commitments, disbursements and balances across the grant portfolio. Supports the Community Liaison Officers and Programme Assistant in following up on grantee financial documentation and reporting. Budget Development and Monitoring; Contributes to the development and periodic revision of the TAZA project budget, ensuring alignment with EU requirements and approved activity plans. Monitors budget execution and spending rates against the approved project budget and work plan, flagging over- or under-expenditure and recommending corrective action. Notifies the Programme Manager and Regional Grants and Contracts Manager of significant budget variances or reallocations requiring EU Delegation approval. Supports the preparation of budget notes and narratives for donor reporting and for any requested contract amendments, cost extensions or no-cost extensions. Maintains accurate and accessible budget-monitoring records for the project. Compliance and Capacity Building; Ensures compliance with IUCN and EU donor financial and grant management requirements, including procurement, financial regulation and reporting rules, when reviewing expenditure and preparing financial reports. Applies IUCN anti-fraud, conflict-of-interest and safeguarding requirements in grant and procurement processes, and promptly reports any suspected irregularity, in line with IUCN policy and the EU grant agreement. Stays up to date on IUCN and EU financial and grants regulations and communicates relevant changes to the project team. Provides guidance and light-touch support to grantees on financial reporting, record keeping, and co-financing documentation, working closely with the project's incubator and capacity-building component. Contributes to the development and improvement of project-level financial management tools and systems. Supports periodic financial monitoring visits to grantees and field sites, in coordination with the Community Liaison Officers. Procurement Support; Supports procurement processes for goods, services and consultancies under TAZA, in coordination with the Regional Procurement and Operations Manager, ensuring procedures are followed and documentation is properly filed. Verifies invoices and supporting documents for goods and services procured under the project prior to clearance and payment. Other Duties; Provides technical guidance and mentorship to project support staff (e.g. Programme Officer Community Liaison Officers) on financial procedures, grant compliance and record keeping. As the Malawi Country Office programme and grant portfolio grow, contributes to extending sound financial and grants management practices to additional grants and projects in the country portfolio, as assigned. Supports the Programme Manager, Regional Grants and Contracts Manager and the Regional Accounting and Compliance Manager on all financial and grants matters relating to the project. Contributes to project inception, mid-term and final review processes, and to donor reporting, as required. Carries out any other relevant tasks assigned by the line manager, consistent with the level of the position. Requirements POSITION REQUIREMENTS; Education; Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a related field. A professional accounting qualification (e.g. ACCA, CIMA, CA(M)) is an added advantage. Work Experience; Minimum 7 years of relevant experience in a grants and/or finance role, preferably within a large or international NGO or donor-funded project, including experience operating at a senior or supervisory level. Experience with EU-funded grants and contracts is required; familiarity with the EU Financial Regulation (including EU regulations on financial support to third parties) and EU grant management procedures is highly desirable. Experience processing payments, verifying financial reports, and maintaining audit-ready documentation. Experience supporting matching-grants or re-granting schemes to MSMEs, community-based organisations or individual entrepreneurs is an advantage. Working knowledge of accounting/ERP software (e.g. Microsoft Dynamics NAV, Business Central etc). Experience providing guidance or mentorship to junior finance, grants or project support staff is an advantage. Language Proficiency; Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of Chichewa is an advantage. Core Competencies; Transparency: Able to build trust and contribute to informed and responsible decision making by carrying out the work of IUCN in a transparent manner; provides clear guidance to ensure that objectives and desired measurable results are understood by members of the team. Inclusiveness: Understands and accepts cultural diversity, and provides a tolerant, positive and supportive working environment that fosters respect for diversity, demonstrates ability to work in a multicultural, multiethnic environment and to maintain effective working relations with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds. Professionalism: Promotes the organization's interests, objectives and values in a diligent and professional manner. Accountability: Takes responsibility for individual and collective actions and promotes the IUCN One Programme approach. Functional Competencies; Strong analytical skills with attention to detail. Team player with strong interpersonal and communication skills. Works effectively with people from different backgrounds. Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple grant files and deadlines. Strong Microsoft Office skills, especially in Excel. Sound understanding of financial analysis, budgeting and financial reporting. Willingness and ability to travel within Malawi to project sites and grantee locations. Applicants will be asked to create an account and submit their profile information. Applications will not be accepted after the closing date. The vacancy closes at midnight, Swiss time (GMT+1 / GMT+2 during Daylight Saving Time, DST). Please note that only selected applicants will be personally contacted for interviews. Other job opportunities are published in the IUCN website: https://www.iucn.org/involved/jobs/ About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 16,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN
